_readme: The declared state of the Fab listing. tools/fab_readiness.py measures the built package
against this, so a field left null is reported as an OPEN DECISION rather than silently
passing. Nothing here is filled in on anyone's behalf: every null below is a question only
Andre can answer, and answering it in this file is what makes it checkable afterwards.
Clause numbers refer to the Fab Distribution Agreement of 23 February 2026.
_listingPrice: 1(d): your complete discretion, but it must be $0.00 or >= $0.99.
_createdWithAI: 18(k)(ii): REQUIRED where 'a material portion of the Content is generated with Generative AI
Programs'. Not a preference. A material portion of this plugin was written by a generative
model, so the honest answer is almost certainly true - but 'material' is a human judgement and
this file will not make it for you. If you set false, say why in createdWithAIReason.
_publishedCommit: The git commit the live Fab listing was built from. 3(b) parity is measured against it.
_otherChannels: 3(b): 'If your Content is made available to end users through channels other than the
Marketplaces, you will provide any Updates to Epic no later than you provide them to any other
third party.' List every channel that reaches an END USER. A private repo only you can pull
from is not one; a private repo three collaborators pull from is. So is an SDK installer that
_licenceInPayload: 3(f)(v): 'content distributed through Fab is licensed only under the Fab End User License
Agreement, which is not superseded by custom licenses included in Content's distributed files'.
The repo's LICENSE is MIT and the repo is public, so every version pushed so far is MIT to
everyone who has it - irrevocably. That cannot be undone, only changed going forward. What CAN
be fixed is the copy inside the Fab package, which must not tell a buyer they have MIT rights.
